approaches.advancement: Proposed: clearest causal continuity with atmosphere and a satisfying physical-to-angular payoff.
approaches.captions: Full narration-faithful phrase coverage in Source Sans 3; integrated spatial labels and a persistent four-step numerical chain; no per-word bounce.
factualProvenanceRisks: H4 must be reconstructed against the verified museum object, not a later boxed chronometer.
Abstract ship indicates navigation, not a named historical voyage.
Explanatory 14:00 label must not masquerade as an H4 24-hour dial.
approaches.feasibility: Feasible with authored 2.5D layers and deterministic motion after approval. A later renderer/typography implementation is needed; no production components exist for this story.
approaches.narration: Warm, precise, conversational English; provisional Kokoro bf_emma candidate, no performed antiquarian accent.
approaches.sound: No music. Very low original ocean room tone for the opening, a few dry object/tick accents outside spoken numerical phrases, silence at comparison.
strengths: Continuity lets the audience track reference versus local reading without relearning a new layout.
Material objects provide atmosphere while abstraction declares an explanatory model.
Globe and angle occupy the same navigational world; no documentary-to-diagram rupture.
approaches.thesis: A clock becomes a spatial explanation through one coherent navigational workbench.
approaches.viewerExperience: Tactile curiosity becomes an aha moment: two readings turn into a visible eastward angular offset.
approaches.visualLanguage: Original non-photoreal 2.5D objects, matte ivory diagram surface, shallow relief water, carefully modeled watch silhouette and globe meridians. One world with stable datum relationships.
weaknesses: Shadows or perspective can make angular geometry misleading unless the proof view is planar.
Original relief artwork and instrument silhouette require new work; not a drop-in scene.

approaches.advancement: Strong alternative if tactile composition tests obscure the mechanism; not selected because object continuity adds meaning without requiring historical dramatization.
approaches.captions: Narration and information share a carefully separated typographic hierarchy; exact spoken coverage still required.
factualProvenanceRisks: Stylized orbit must not imply sidereal-day conversion.
H4 reduction may make watch identity too generic.
approaches.feasibility: Straightforward original 2D implementation after direction approval, but existing renderer convenience is not an editorial advantage.
approaches.narration: Crisp contemporary explainer delivery; numerical contrast leads rather than historical atmosphere.
approaches.sound: Silence under voice with restrained synthetic confirmation accents, no ambience or music.
strengths: Lowest reconstruction and external-image rights burden.
approaches.thesis: The viewer watches time itself become an angular coordinate.
approaches.viewerExperience: An immediate puzzle resolves through typography, linked readouts and a spare circle of meridians.
approaches.visualLanguage: Entirely abstract 2D editorial typography and geometric motion; historical H4 represented by a minimal factual label or silhouette.
weaknesses: May feel like a classroom equation rather than a discovery.
Less sense of why keeping time at sea mattered.
Strong convergence risk with familiar procedural Magnivis scale/number graphics.

approaches.advancement: Not selected: emotional atmosphere is strong, but the mechanism needs a unified explanatory space rather than a compressed period drama.
approaches.captions: Conventional full phrase subtitles supplemented by explanatory labels, kept away from historical instruments.
factualProvenanceRisks: Fictitious crew, ship or readings could be mistaken for an actual H4 trial.
Museum photography needs an explicit license, despite the object being historical.
Atmospheric montage can hide simultaneous time and mean-time corrections.
approaches.feasibility: Higher cost and rights review; photoreal reconstruction cannot be treated as historical footage. No media generation/download authorized.
approaches.narration: Measured documentary storyteller; warmth without theatrical historical impersonation.
approaches.sound: Carefully sourced maritime ambience and a restrained non-melodic music bed, removed for the numerical proof.
strengths: Immediate maritime stakes and historical texture.
Museum imagery could ground instrument identity.
approaches.thesis: An eighteenth-century ship holds two kinds of time while its position remains uncertain.
approaches.viewerExperience: A human-scale maritime scene opens into an explanatory account of longitude.
approaches.visualLanguage: Photoreal reconstruction, macro watch imagery and archival material with separately identified explanatory geometry.
weaknesses: Full causal comparison would require cuts between documentary imagery and analytical views.
Unnecessary ship/clothing specificity creates research and art burdens.
At 41–47 seconds a biography or voyage vignette competes with the central mechanism.

selectionMethod: Editorial judgment against approved comprehension contract; no numerical winner or generated sample.
